content:
ali: Heads-up: compliance flagged private deploy logs - they want WAF events tied to archive CMK for audits. Where should we put key identifiers? cc @maria
maria: We should not put any plaintext key material in logs. Key identifiers (alias or key_id) are fine, plus request_id for correlation.
ben: Current pipeline: edge-waf -> forwarder -> splunk. Forwarder can call keystore metadata API to get alias. But we must limit perms.
ali: Agreed. Proposal: metadata-only endpoint `/keystore/v1/metadata?alias=` that returns only `key_id` and `arn`. No decrypt.
maria: That reduces blast radius. Create IAM role `keystore.metadata-reader` and give forwarder service-account that role.
ben: I'll raise the IAM PR and add a CI smoke test that attempts Decrypt with that SA and expects 403.
ops-bot: Ticket created: INFRA-1246 (rbac: forwarder -> keystore.metadata-reader) assigned to @ben.
ali: For Splunk, create index `priv-deploy-waf` with 2y retention and SSE-KMS on archived exports. Include `archive_manifest.json` with `cmk_arn` and time range.
maria: For the recent WAF upgrade (CVE-2026-1029) we need evidence: 1) Splunk query for events with `key_id` 2) forwarder call logs showing metadata fetches 3) keystore audit logs showing metadata-reader calls 4) no decrypt calls by forwarder.
ben: I'll add a runbook section with those steps and example Splunk queries. Example: `index=priv-deploy-waf key_id=alias/priv-deploy-01 | stats count by waf_rule, action`
ali: Also add a short post-patch validation: sample logs, forwarder trace ids, and keystore audit export. Compliance can sign off with those artifacts.
maria: Sounds good. Ben, ping here when PR is up and CI smoke test passes.
ben: PR: https://git.company/repo/pulls/501 (rbac/keystore-metadata-forwarder). CI tests queued.
ops-bot: CI status: queued.
ali: Thanks team. We'll file the audit evidence after CI green.
